name: Gulf of the Farallones
where: The ocean outside the Golden Gate, California
say: Out under the bridge and over the bar: shipping lanes, Point Reyes, Bodega Bay and the Farallon Islands 27 miles off

layers.wind: Recorded. NOAA HRRR 3 km analyses, one an hour, 08:00 PDT 26 July 2024 for 36 hours. Not the Bay's day: on 14 and 15 July the ocean was nearly calm, and this water wants its north-wester. Baked on a 4 km grid over the whole water.
layers.stream: Recorded. NOAA SFBOFS from the Golden Gate out to about 45 km and north to Point Reyes; beyond it (the Farallones, Bodega, the south-west corner) NOAA WCOFS, the 4 km West Coast model, mixed in over the last 5 km of the finer model's water. 1 km grid, with a 250 m inset over the Gate and the bar.
layers.tide: Recorded. SFBOFS water level at San Francisco (Presidio), the Bay's own station. One tide for the whole water: Bodega and Point Reyes are really about half an hour ahead of it.
layers.depth: SFBOFS model depths where it has water, Terrarium elevation tiles elsewhere. 200 m grid, with finer insets over the Gate and bar (100 m), Bodega Harbour (25 m), Southeast Farallon, Pillar Point and Bolinas (50 m). Two dredged channels are cut in by rule: the main ship channel over the bar at its charted 55 feet, and Bodega Harbour's, deeper and wider than life.
layers.land: Terrarium elevation tiles. 200 m grid, with 80 m insets over the Golden Gate, Bodega Head, Point Reyes and Pillar Point and 40 m over Southeast Farallon.
layers.swell: Recorded, as a declaration: the `sea` block above is the north-west sea NOAA's GFS wave model had off the Gate for these 36 hours, averaged (1.2 m at 8 s from 292). sea.json holds the model's hourly figures, the southerly swell beside it, and a typical July swell. Open fetch 300 km: west of the chart is the open Pacific.
layers.fog: Not drawn. The Bay draws a fixed bank of marine layer where this water is sailed, so that piece is left off here. features.json says what this water wants of the fog.
